messages:
alex.dev: Quick sync — thinking through policy engine placement for edge routing (decisions need latency/cost/region/tier awareness). Two high-level approaches: sidecar policy process per node vs in-runtime policy evaluation. I want to capture tradeoffs and a short sim plan.

maria: Sidecar gives independent hot-reloads and richer plugins, but watch RPC tail latency (esp cold reconnections). Also ops surface increases.

raj_p: In-runtime wins on obvious p90/p99 latency (no RPC hop) and simpler observability for request traces. Downsides: deploys are riskier, policy bugs can crash routing process.

samir: Hybrid thought — keep a tiny in-runtime fast path for simple rules (region, tier, static weights) and offload costly scoring (model-based or eval-heavy) to sidecar. Fallback to static rules if sidecar slow.

alex.dev: Agree on hybrid being interesting. We need numbers: cost of an extra RPC vs the latency savings from not running heavy evals inline. Plan to run a quick sim: 10k requests across 3 regions, mix of short and long sequences, with sidecar latency distribution [5ms median, 40ms tail] vs in-runtime eval cost ~6ms median, 25ms tail.

maria: Add to sim: include network variance (10ms jitter) and a cold-start scenario where sidecar process is recycled. We saw this cause +30ms in a beta test.

raj_p: Also capture batching effects. In-runtime can batch many fast checks without RPC aggregation. Sidecar could expose a batch endpoint but adds queuing latency.

ops-jen: From ops: Canarying policy changes is easier with sidecar (roll forward individual nodes). But policies that change decision shapes will cause traffic variance — add traffic shaping to the sim.

alex.dev: Small config sketch for the hybrid path — putting it here so sims use consistent inputs:

```
policy:
  fast_path:
    rules: [region_pref, tier_priority, static_affinity]
  heavy_path:
    adapter: sidecar_rpc
    timeout_ms: 50
  fallback: fast_path
```

samir: For realism, make heavy_path timeout adapt based on current p95 of sidecar RPC — if >40ms, lower to 30ms and escalate to fallback.

maria: Metric list for sim: per-decision latency histogram, percent decisions served by fast_path vs heavy_path, sidecar rpc p50/p95/p99, routing request tail latency, error rates when heavy_path times out.

raj_p: I'll instrument a lightweight adapter and run the batch vs inline microbench. Expectation: inline wins under low CPU, sidecar wins when we need polyglot plugins (python scoring) or third-party evals.

ci-bot: quick note: started a sim job #sim-176987 (10k reqs, regional skew = us-west:70%, eu:20%, apac:10%). Results will post here when finished. :robot_face: 

ops-jen: If sim shows heavy tail from sidecar, we should prototype a shadow mode where decisions are made both inline and via sidecar and compare outputs/latency for N=1M requests.

alex.dev: Good call. Action items: raj_p to produce adapter + microbench by EOD, maria to add metrics and run sim config, samir to implement adaptive timeout knob, ops-jen to draft canary/rollback checklist for sidecar changes. We'll reconvene after sim results.

maria: acked — adding dashboard to show fast_path vs heavy_path split.

raj_p: ack, starting adapter now.

ci-bot: sim job #sim-176987 queued (ETA ~12m).

alex.dev: Thanks all — want a brief follow-up thread with sim numbers and recommendation (keep hybrid, inline-only, or sidecar-first).

samir: +1, prefer hybrid if sim shows <=5% requests hitting heavy_path under typical traffic.

ops-jen: tagging infra to watch node CPU if we go inline-heavy: @infra-team.

ci-bot: sim job #sim-176987 completed. Results: fast_path handled ~82% of decisions, heavy_path p95=48ms, sidecar timeouts=0.4%. Posting detailed run artifacts to the sim bucket. :white_check_mark:
